A result under 15 percent is considered reassuring, 15 to 30 percent sits in a grey zone, and above 30 percent shapes the protocol directly, often prompting ICSI with IMSI selection or testicular sperm retrieval. Difficulty conceiving a year after pregnancy loss often traces back to identifiable causes, uterine fibroids, polyps, or a septum obstructing implantation; thyroid disorders affecting both fertility and miscarriage risk; or luteal phase insufficiency where progesterone levels are inadequate to sustain the uterine lining. Each of these is investigable through targeted testing. Dr. Mohit Saraogi, an IVF doctor in Ghatkopar, conducts this structured evaluation for patients who have not conceived within twelve months of loss.

Ovulatory dysfunction is among the most common causes of female infertility, when the ovaries fail to release an egg on schedule, often linked to PCOS or thyroid imbalance, there is simply no egg available for fertilisation that cycle. Blocked fallopian tubes and uterine abnormalities such as fibroids or polyps are the other leading structural causes. Dr. Mohit Saraogi, an infertility specialist in Ghatkopar, investigates each of these systematically before recommending any treatment pathway.

Couples typically undergo two to three IUI cycles before their fertility specialist reassesses the treatment plan a single attempt rarely determines whether the approach is working for a given diagnosis. Per-cycle outcomes vary depending on age, sperm parameters, and the underlying cause of infertility. Dr. Mohit Saraogi, who provides IUI Treatment in Ghatkopar, discusses realistic cycle expectations with every patient and recommends IVF when IUI cycles do not achieve the intended result.

Research across millions of IVF births consistently shows no clinically significant difference in the cognitive, physical, or psychological development of IVF-conceived children compared to those conceived naturally. From the point of uterine implantation, the developmental pathway is identical — the only difference in IVF is where fertilisation takes place. Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre, an IVF specialist in Ghatkopar, addresses health outcome concerns at every consultation before any treatment decision is made.

Uterine structural issues polyps, submucosal fibroids, and intrauterine adhesions — can sit undetected on standard ultrasound and silently fail transfers with good-quality embryos until a hysteroscopy is performed. The ERA test identifies a displaced implantation window in approximately 25% of patients with repeated failure, shifting transfer timing by a full day or more. An IVF doctor in Ghatkopar, Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre conducts a full case review after every failed transfer before any next step is confirmed.

IUI bypasses the cervical stage of natural conception entirely — washed, concentrated sperm are placed directly into the uterine cavity through a thin catheter timed to coincide with confirmed ovulation. In natural conception, sperm must navigate the cervix independently, a process that filters out a significant proportion. The procedure takes under 10 minutes without anaesthesia. Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre provides IUI Treatment in Ghatkopar following a full diagnostic workup before any protocol is started.

Chromosomal abnormality rates in embryos rise sharply with maternal age — at 40, more than half of embryos may be aneuploid even when morphology appears normal on visual grading. PGT-A addresses this gap by screening chromosome count before transfer, reducing the chance of selecting a non-viable embryo. As an IVF specialist in Ghatkopar, Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre applies PGT-A only when the clinical indication is clear — not as a default recommendation for all patients undergoing treatment.

AMH measures ovarian reserve but says nothing directly about egg quality or pregnancy likelihood. What it does tell a fertility specialist is how the ovaries will respond to stimulation and what dosage to begin with. Normal AMH ranges vary significantly by age: 2.5–5.0 ng/mL at 25–30, dropping to 0.5–2.5 ng/mL between 36 and 40. At the IVF Centre in Ghatkopar, Saraogi Hospital reads AMH alongside antral follicle count and full hormonal panels before any cycle is planned or recommended.

When you are struggling to conceive, navigating the world of fertility treatments can feel overwhelming. Patients often visit our center asking to understand the difference between IVF vs IUI treatment. Making the right choice is crucial for both your emotional well-being and your finances.

IUI (Intrauterine Insemination) or artificial insemination, is often a first-line treatment where washed sperm is placed directly into the uterus during ovulation. It is less invasive and ideal for mild male factor or unexplained infertility. However, if you are dealing with blocked fallopian tubes, severe endometriosis, or male infertility, the test tube baby procedure (IVF) offers significantly higher success rates. In IVF, fertilization happens in our advanced lab before the embryo is transferred back. At Govinda IVF, the best fertility clinic in Ghatkopar, we don’t believe in guesswork. Having diabetes doesn’t mean you can’t conceive. It means your fertility journey needs the right preparation. 🌻💛

Uncontrolled blood sugar levels can impact fertility in both men and women:

• Men: reduced sperm count, poor motility, and increased sperm DNA fragmentation

🌻 Optimise blood sugar levels and HbA1c (as advised by your doctor)
🌻 Consult both an endocrinologist and a fertility specialist
🌻 Review medications, nutrition, and lifestyle factors that affect reproductive health

Choosing the right IVF clinic is one of the most important decisions in your fertility journey. The right center not only offers advanced treatments but also provides transparency, trust, and personalised care at every step.

Many couples try to conceive naturally for months or even years before seeking medical advice. However, certain signs may indicate that it is the right time to consult a fertility specialist for proper evaluation and guidance.

One of the most common signs is trying for pregnancy for a long time without success. If a couple has been trying to conceive for over a year without results, or for six months if the woman is above 35, it may be time to seek medical support. Early consultation can help identify underlying causes and avoid delays in treatment.

Irregular menstrual cycles are another important indicator. Conditions such as hormonal imbalance or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) can affect ovulation and reduce the chances of natural conception. A specialist can assess these issues and recommend appropriate care.

Male fertility factors are also an important part of fertility evaluation. Low sperm count, poor motility, or other sperm-related concerns can affect conception. Foods to Avoid During IVF Treatment

Nutrition plays an important role during fertility care. While there is no strict “IVF diet,” certain foods are better avoided to support better outcomes and overall health during treatment.

Highly processed foods such as packaged snacks, fried items, and fast food should be limited. These foods are often high in trans fats, refined sugar, and preservatives that may affect hormonal balance. Excess sugar intake can also impact insulin levels, which is especially important for women with PCOS.

It is advisable to reduce caffeine consumption from coffee, energy drinks, and certain soft drinks. High caffeine intake may affect implantation in some cases. Alcohol should also be avoided during fertility treatment, as it can interfere with hormonal regulation and egg quality.

Raw or undercooked foods, including unpasteurised dairy, raw eggs, or uncooked seafood, should be avoided to reduce the risk of infection.

 High-mercury fish such as shark or swordfish are also not recommended. Maintaining a balanced diet supports the body during IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments and helps create a healthier environment for conception.

Separating Truth from Myths About IVF

IVF is one of the most effective fertility treatments today, yet many myths create confusion and unnecessary fear. Understanding the facts helps couples take timely and confident decisions.

A common myth is that IVF always guarantees pregnancy. The fact is that IVF improves the chances of conception, but success depends on factors such as age, egg quality, sperm health, and overall medical condition. 

Another misconception is that IVF is extremely painful. In reality, most procedures are well-managed with modern techniques and patient-focused care, making them comfortable and safe.

Many believe IVF is only meant for women with severe fertility problems. In truth, IVF is advised for multiple conditions, including male infertility, blocked fallopian tubes, endometriosis, repeated miscarriages, and unexplained infertility. 

There is also a belief that IVF always results in twins or triplets. With careful embryo selection and transfer, the risk of multiple pregnancy is controlled.

Egg retrieval is one of the most important steps in the IVF process. It is a carefully planned medical procedure where mature eggs are collected from the ovaries so they can be fertilised in a laboratory. Understanding this step helps reduce fear and builds confidence before starting treatment.

Before egg retrieval, the ovaries are stimulated using fertility medications to help multiple eggs mature at the same time. During this phase, ultrasound scans and blood tests are done regularly to monitor follicle growth and hormone levels. Once the eggs (follicles) are ready, ovum pick-up (OPU) is timed very precisely after the trigger injection.

Male fertility problems are equally common and often misunderstood. Lifestyle factors such as stress, smoking, obesity, and medical conditions can also impact male fertility.

RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology adds an additional layer of electronic witnessing by assigning unique identifiers to biological samples and tracking them through key stages of the IVF process. This helps strengthen traceability and supports laboratory protocols designed to minimise the possibility of mix-ups.
At Nova IVF Fertility, RFID-based witnessing is integrated into our IVF laboratory processes as part of our commitment to maintaining high standards of safety and care.

featured_reviews.review_text:
While trying to conceive, we had been through all the regular routes, homeopathy, ayurveda, HRT, IUI. Something about IVF made us feel that maybe it wasn’t the best way ahead for us. But the truth is, we probably needed to get to it sooner to save ourselves the prolonged disappointment and get closure either-way.

I believe we met Dr. Anand at the right time in our lives, thanks to friends of ours who had just delivered their babies under his care. We were immediately put at ease when we met him. Unlike some of the biggest doctors we met, who put me through some very unnecessary and discouraging tests, Dr.Anand asked us to put all that in the back burner & start afresh with complete faith. He was always very realistic and practical about the options and odds he presented us with. No false promises, no pessimism either.

He caught something in one of my reports that no one else had so far and with a small procedure we took care of it and marched towards our transfer. We were blessed to have conceived in our first attempt. It was such a surreal and special moment.

But the journey didn’t get any easier. I had minor bleeding incidents in the first trimester & Dr. Anand was always accessible and responsive in administering the best protocol to safeguard the pregnancy. In the 22nd week, after everything seemed under control, I went to visit my family in Chennai. During that time, some odd symptoms pushed me to go for a Scan where we found out that I was almost fully dilated and had to be taken in for an emergency cerclage & pessary placement. All these words just flew over my head. But something kept me very calm and strong, I knew I had to keep it together for the baby and not make things worse by panicking. featured_reviews.name: Isha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience with Dr. Anand has been incredible. I am 41 and have just been blessed with a baby girl delivered by Dr. Anand through IVF procedure.

At advanced maternal age, after 2 miscarriages, existing adenomyosis/endometriosis and with potentially poor quality of eggs due to medical history, I was certain of not just relying on trial and error through natural conception. We knew IVF was the way forward for us.

We tried IVF procedure at other clinics and met many doctors before making this critical decision of trusting Dr. Anand with our journey.

IVF procedure requires a lot of time, patience and commitment from both doctor and patient - I underwent 3 IVF cycles to finally achieve 4 usable embryos at Dr. Anand’s clinic. I also underwent medically induced menopause and hysteroscopy to reduce the impact of pre-existing adenomyosis/endometriosis before we went ahead with embryo transfer. Successful conception happened in the 2nd cycle of embryo transfer. The IVF medications continued till end of 4th month to support the pregnancy.

It was physically, emotionally, mentally and financially demanding journey. We completely trusted Dr. Anand's expertise and he has been our guide through this journey.

What was great during this journey ?
We have been with Benzer and Dr. Anand since 2023 and he was always available at all times and promptly and patiently answered all our queries. He would spend time with us explaining every step of journey and gently guiding us through the steps - right from the medications to the injections to the final delivery,  he was with us. This really helps as our treatment was complex and each patient believes they are different.

What you should be prepared for ?
Patience, Mental Strength and Faith - This is a journey with lots of ups and downs but the reward at the end of this journey would be that sweet bundle of happiness you call your own.
